meta.title: Norwegian B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Norwegian → English (see the Norwegian, recall the meaning) and English → Norwegian (see an English meaning, recall the Norwegian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words of Norwegian Bokmål — the written standard most Norwegians use — for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise whilst travelling, to produce simple connected text on topics which are familiar or of personal interest, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Norway examines learners at these levels — Norskprøven and Bergenstesten — but neither was found to publish a word list, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 235 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — work and the economy, society and politics, media and technology, the environment, education, relationships and family life, home and housing, health, travel and experiences, culture and leisure, feelings and opinions, the words of explaining and arguing, the verbs and adjectives of judging, time and frequency, and the connectors that build an argument — and the other 765 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Norwegian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. The 556 nouns are printed with their article — en, ei or et, and en/ei where Bokmål allows either — because the article is the gender, which decides the noun's definite ending, the adjective's ending and the pronoun that stands for it, and they show their definite singular and their plural (bilen, biler); the 249 verbs show their present, past and past participle, the forms a Norwegian verb is learnt by (spiser, spiste, spist), and behind the All forms fold their imperative, passive and participles. Real example sentences come with 760 of the 1000 words, three apiece for 428 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

There is no such thing, at this stage of the world’s history in The United States of America, as an independent press. You know it and I know it. There is not one of you who dare write your honest opinions, and if you did, you know beforehand that it would never appear in print. I am paid weekly for keeping my honest opinions out of the paper I am connected with. Others of you are paid similar salaries for similar things, and any of you who would be foolish as to write honest opinions would be out on the streets looking for another job. If I allowed my honest opinions to appear in one issue of my papers, before twenty-four hours my occupation would be gone. The business of the journalist is to destroy the truth, to lie outright, to pervert, to vilify, to fawn at the feet of Mammon, and to sell his country and his race for his daily bread. Impa's at the hospital. Ganon—" Suddenly the King heard an incomprehensible cry and turned around to see Fari rush past him. "Damn, Fari, what was that?!" "Piss off, Your Majesty!" Fari yelled at the top of his lungs. "My... PMSing as usual, I see," the King continued to mutter dejectedly. "Shit, I'm so fucking bored. Nothing good on TV. Nothing good online.
